topic: effect of each listed rear sprocket (calculated)
statement: Worked out from the 2021 EC 250 / EC 300 stock 14:52 gearing, each manufacturer-listed rear sprocket changes every gear's overall ratio by: 14:45 -13.5%, 14:48 -7.7%, 14:49 -5.8%, 14:50 -3.8%, 14:51 -1.9%, 14:52 0.0% (positive = shorter gearing, more acceleration and less top speed; one rear tooth is roughly 2%).
notes: Change = (new rear / front) / (stock rear / front) - 1, front sprocket unchanged.

statement: Worked out from the 2027 TX 300 stock 14:48 gearing, each manufacturer-listed rear sprocket changes every gear's overall ratio by: 14:48 0.0%, 14:49 +2.1% (positive = shorter gearing, more acceleration and less top speed; one rear tooth is roughly 2%).
notes: Change = (new rear / front) / (stock rear / front) - 1, front sprocket unchanged.

statement: Worked out from Husqvarna's 2027 TX 300 gear ratios (TX model): rpm drops on each upshift are about 1st-2nd 26.1%, 2nd-3rd 23.0%, 3rd-4th 18.2%, 4th-5th 15.4%, 5th-6th 15.4%, and the overall spread from 1st to 6th is 3.0:1. Larger drops mean the engine falls further down its powerband after a shift.
notes: Drop = 1 - ratio(n+1)/ratio(n), the fractional rpm fall when shifting up at constant road speed.

notes: Measured on the SX sister model. The 2023 owner's manuals list identical bore, stroke, Z dimension and primary drive for the 300 SX, 300 XC and TX 300, but XC/TX ECU calibration and gearing differ, so treat the figure as indicative.

source.name: Dirt Rider - How Much Power Does the 2023 KTM 300 SX Make? (Dynojet 250i)

topic: second dyno source: 2023 300 TBI engine (300 SX, different dyno)
statement: A second magazine dyno measured the stock 2023 KTM 300 SX at 54.96 hp at 8,560 rpm and 35.38 lb-ft at 7,450 rpm on the green map; testers called the stock delivery linear and "luggy" low to mid with little bottom hit. Different dynos read differently, so compare only within one source.
notes: Same engine family as the 2023 300 XC / TX 300 (shared owner's-manual engine data). Kept side by side with the 48.8 hp reading from another dyno - see conflicts.

source.name: Motocross Action - MXA team tested: FMF 2023 KTM 250/300SX pipe/silencer

topic: rear-wheel dyno: 2025 300 TBI engine (measured on the 300 SX)

topic: manufacturer description of power and maps: 2026 300 XC
statement: KTM describes the 2026 300 XC as a 300 cc two-stroke for racers wanting maximum power at the least weight, with two maps on the standard switch: Map 1 gives linear, predictable delivery and Map 2 "crisp, explosive power output"; weight without fuel is listed as 101.8 kg.

topic: manufacturer description of power and maps: 2024 300 XC
statement: KTM says the 2024 300 XC comes with a map select switch as standard: Map 1 for linear, predictable power and Map 2 for crisp, explosive output; the power valve is auto-calibrating so it never needs adjusting. Weight without fuel 102.1 kg.

source.name: KTM Canada model page - 2024 KTM 300 XC (French)

topic: manufacturer description of power and maps: 2027 125 XC
statement: KTM describes the 2027 125 XC as unmatched power with lightweight construction; a standard map switch gives Map 1 (linear, predictable) and Map 2 (more aggressive); weight without fuel 94.8 kg.

source.name: KTM USA model page - 2027 KTM 125 XC

topic: manufacturer description of power and maps: 2023 125 XC
statement: KTM says the 2023 125 XC likes to rev but is surprisingly responsive when needed, and claims more torque than any 125 cc two-stroke before it; Mode 1 gives linear, predictable delivery and Mode 2 more explosive power. Weight without fuel 93.1 kg.

source.name: KTM Canada model page - 2023 KTM 125 XC (French)

topic: manufacturer description of power and maps: 2026 300 XC-W
statement: KTM describes the 2026 300 XC-W engine as delivering "masses of low-down torque and top-end fury"; Map 1 is the standard linear, predictable map and Map 2 a more aggressive map for added throttle response, selectable only with the optional Map Select switch.

source.name: KTM USA model page - 2026 KTM 300 XC-W

topic: manufacturer description of power and maps: 2025 250 XC-W
statement: KTM claims the 2025 250 XC-W engine makes more torque than any previous 250 two-stroke; TBI is tuned for the smoothest, most consistent delivery in gnarly conditions; Map 1 is linear and predictable, Map 2 crisper and more explosive via the optional switch.

source.name: KTM Canada model page - 2025 KTM 250 XC-W

topic: manufacturer description of power and maps: 2025 150 XC-W
statement: KTM calls the 2025 150 XC-W 'in a class of its own' with a fiery, fast-responding engine; electronically controlled TBI with a 39 mm Keihin throttle body aims for smooth, consistent delivery, and the optional map switch selects Map 1 (linear, predictable) or Map 2 (more aggressive). Weight without fuel 97.8 kg.

source.name: KTM USA model page - 2025 KTM 150 XC-W

topic: manufacturer description of power and maps: 2026 150 XC-W
statement: KTM calls the 2026 150 XC-W 'in a class of its own' with a fiery, fast-responding engine; electronically controlled TBI with a 39 mm Keihin throttle body aims for smooth, consistent delivery, and the optional map switch selects Map 1 (linear, predictable) or Map 2 (more aggressive). Weight without fuel 96.4 kg.

source.name: KTM New Zealand model page - 2026 KTM 150 XC-W

topic: manufacturer description of power and maps: 2027 150 XC-W
statement: KTM calls the 2027 150 XC-W 'in a class of its own' with a fiery, fast-responding engine; electronically controlled TBI with a 39 mm Keihin throttle body aims for smooth, consistent delivery, and the optional map switch selects Map 1 (linear, predictable) or Map 2 (more aggressive). Weight without fuel 96.4 kg.

source.name: KTM USA model page - 2027 KTM 150 XC-W

statement: Husqvarna says the 2024 TE 300 gains torque while keeping its high-revving character; a new 39 mm throttle body with dual injectors is positioned for more immediate response; Map 1 gives predictable linear power and Map 2 added throttle response.

source.name: Husqvarna Motorcycles model page - TE 300 2024

statement: Husqvarna says the 2026 TE 150 makes impressive torque for a small two-stroke with usable enduro power; Map 1 (white) is linear and progressive for hard-pack, Map 2 (green) is more aggressive for sand and heavy conditions. Weight without fuel 100 kg, seat height 952 mm.

source.name: Husqvarna Motorcycles USA model page - TE 150 2026

topic: manufacturer claims for the 2024 TBI enduro engines
statement: KTM said the 2024 TBI system gives "almost carburetor levels of ultra-smooth power delivery" and that the electronic power valve improves mid-range power; the 150, 250 and 300 all use a 39 mm Keihin throttle body and a 6-speed wide-ratio gearbox.
notes: Manufacturer release as reported by the magazine.

source.name: Cycle News - New 2024 KTM XC-W two-stroke off-road model specs (KTM release)

statement: Test riders found the 2024 150 XC-W pulls well low in Map 1 (you have to be a couple of gears off to bog it), builds linearly with revs with little over-rev and no sharp hit; Map 2 gets into the power faster for climbs; the TBI fueling was described as flawless.
notes: Professional test-rider impressions, not measurements.

source.name: Ultimate Motorcycling - 2024 KTM XC-W lineup test (300, 250 and 150 reviewed)

statement: Test riders found the 2024 250 XC-W has power across the whole range matched to the 6-speed, with the damped clutch softening delivery for traction; Map 2 is a big step more aggressive and can spin the rear tire unexpectedly.
notes: Professional test-rider impressions.

source.name: Ultimate Motorcycling - 2024 KTM XC-W lineup test (300, 250 and 150 reviewed)

statement: Test riders found the 2024 300 XC-W strong from just off idle through the midrange ("tractor-esque"), dropping off when over-revved; Map 1 is calm and nearly impossible to get into trouble with, Map 2 suits fast open terrain but is a handful in tight changes of direction.
notes: Professional test-rider impressions.

source.name: Ultimate Motorcycling - 2024 KTM XC-W lineup test (300, 250 and 150 reviewed)

statement: A tester found the 2022 EX 300 TPI has plenty of power and spot-on throttle response, but wanted a smoother bottom end for slow technical trail and noticed lean spots before the engine reached full temperature.

source.name: Cycle News - 2022 GasGas EX 300 review

statement: A tester described the 2022 EC 300 TPI as a little mellower than the carbureted predecessors, slightly lean-feeling until warm, and able to tractor through rugged terrain; it seemed to run better at high elevation.

source.name: Cycle News - 2022 GasGas EC 300 review

statement: A tester found the 2021 TE 300i makes lots of usable power delivered in a very linear way, all but impossible to stall at low speed; the map switch made a negligible difference, and a slightly lean feel with occasional light detonation under low-rpm load was noted.

source.name: Cycle News - 2021 Husqvarna TE 300i review

topic: test-rider comparison: 2023 300 XC TBI vs 300 XC-W TPI
statement: Comparing project bikes, a tester called the 2023 300 XC TBI "intense" with more torque and horsepower than any previous 300 he had ridden, while the 2023 300 XC-W TPI was smooth and rideable but lacked the bottom-end grunt and midrange pull of the earlier carbureted bikes; he preferred the XC-W for long tight loops.

source.name: Dirt Bike Magazine - Project bike shootout: KTM 300 TPI vs KTM 300 TBI

topic: aftermarket pipe and silencer on the 2023 300 TBI (dyno)
statement: On a magazine dyno an aftermarket pipe and titanium silencer lifted a 2023 KTM 300 SX from 54.96 to 58.08 hp (peak moved from 8,560 to 8,800 rpm) and torque from 35.38 to 36.10 lb-ft, with slightly less power from 5,800 to 6,700 rpm; riders felt more snap and bottom-end hit. The kit is listed for the 2023 250/300 XC and TX 300 as well.

vals.parts: FMF Factory Fatty pipe, titanium Powercore 2.1 silencer

notes: Measured on the 300 SX; fitment to XC/TX stated by the article. On a 2023 TC 250 the same system added just over 1 hp.

source.name: Motocross Action - MXA team tested: FMF 2023 KTM 250/300SX pipe/silencer

statement: On the 2020 TX 300i TPI an aftermarket pipe added about 3 hp at 7,500 rpm and about 3 hp at 9,000 rpm over the stock 48 hp engine.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test: 2020 Husqvarna TX300i

statement: A plug-and-play replacement ECU for TPI KTM, Husqvarna and GasGas two-strokes (tested on a 2022 EC 300 and a 300 XC-W) made the engine run better from the bottom through the range and removed the detonation common on stock 300 TPIs; it also fed more oil and keeps the stock map-switch and warning-light functions. List price $649.99.
notes: Applied to the TPI years of each model only (TPI: 250/300 XC and TX 300 2020-2022, XC-W/TE 2020-2023, GasGas EX/EC 2021-2023). Not tuneable by the owner.

source.name: Cycle News - Coober USA KTM/Husqvarna/GasGas 300 TPI ECU

topic: TPI 300 project: head insert, ECU and suspension
statement: On a 2023 300 XC-W TPI project a high-compression head with a mountain insert added low-end grunt and midrange pull at altitude, and a stock-ECU reflash or replacement ECU gave a big boost in power and torque by correcting the lean fueling - the change the tester would make first.

source.name: Dirt Bike Magazine - Project bike shootout: KTM 300 TPI vs KTM 300 TBI

topic: TBI 300 XC project: making the power manageable
statement: On a 2023 300 XC TBI project the tester added no power; instead an auto clutch and a slower-turning throttle cam made the power more manageable, with flywheel weights planned next, and re-valved or replaced suspension was the biggest improvement.

source.name: Dirt Bike Magazine - Project bike shootout: KTM 300 TPI vs KTM 300 TBI

statement: On the 2022 EX 300 a tester slowed the power-valve opening by a little over a quarter turn to find his sweet spot, and on the EC 300 the power-valve tension is the simple tuning adjustment that replaces the KTM/Husqvarna map switch.
notes: EC statement from the companion EC 300 review.

source.name: Cycle News - 2022 GasGas EX 300 review

topic: fixes for a rough-running 250 XC TPI
statement: For a 2020 250 XC TPI that splutters at part throttle low to mid and runs rich, a magazine suggests turning in the throttle-body air screw from four turns out, asking the dealer for the latest ECU settings, or using a piggyback tuner, replacement ECU, stock-ECU reflash or a fuel-injector relocation package with a new head; it reports great results from a tested replacement ECU.

source.name: Dirt Bike Magazine - KTM 250 TPI issues and solutions (Mr. Know-It-All)

topic: carb baseline for the Mikuni TMX 38 on the 125 XC
statement: One forum member suggests a Yamaha-YZ125-style baseline for the Mikuni TMX 38 on the 2021-22 125 XC: air screw 2-1/4 turns, #40 pilot, 4 mm slide cutaway, 6BFY42-74 needle on the 3rd clip, S-4 needle jet, #410 main and 10 mm float level (sea level, 68 F, 30:1 premix), lowering the fuel level 1.0-1.5 mm for off-road to cut overflow losses.
notes: Single poster, no follow-up results; differs from KTM's stock 125 XC US jetting (main 470, needle 6BFY43-75) - start from the owner's-manual settings.

source.name: ThumperTalk - Jetting the Mikuni TMX carb on 2017-2021 KTM 125/150SX and 2021-22 KTM 125XC

topic: map switch and auto-calibrating power valve: 2024 and 2026 300 XC
statement: KTM fits the 300 XC with a map select switch as standard (Map 1 linear, Map 2 aggressive) and says the electronic exhaust-port control is auto-calibrating, so there are no power-valve adjustments; fueling is Keihin EFI with a Vitesco ECU and needs no jetting.
notes: Same statements appear on the 2024 page.

source.name: KTM USA model page - 2026 KTM 300 XC

statement: KTM fits the 125 XC with a standard map switch for two perceptibly different maps and an electronically controlled, self-calibrating exhaust port; the 2023 model introduced a 39 mm throttle body with the throttle cable acting directly on it for smoother response.

source.name: KTM Canada model page - 2023 KTM 125 XC (French)

topic: optional map switch on TBI XC-W models
statement: KTM sells the Map Select switch as an optional extra on all XC-W models; without it the bikes run Map 1, the standard linear map, while Map 2 adds throttle response.
notes: Stated on the 2025-2027 150/250/300 XC-W model pages.

source.name: KTM USA model page - 2026 KTM 300 XC-W

topic: map switch price and use on the 2024 XC-W range
statement: All 2024 XC-W models ship running Map 1; the Map 2 handlebar switch is an accessory of about $150, which testers recommended for racing on the 250 while leaving tired riders on Map 1.

source.name: Ultimate Motorcycling - 2024 KTM XC-W lineup test (300, 250 and 150 reviewed)

statement: Husqvarna identifies the TE 150 maps by lamp colour: Map 1 white for linear power on hard pack, Map 2 green, more aggressive, for sand and heavy going; oil is fed by an EMS-controlled electronic pump.

source.name: Husqvarna Motorcycles USA model page - TE 150 2026

statement: Husqvarna says the 2024 TE 300 EMS controls an electronic oil pump that meters oil by rpm and load, an electronic exhaust control for the lateral exhaust ports, and a dual-injector 39 mm throttle body; two maps give linear (Map 1) or sharper (Map 2) response.

source.name: Husqvarna Motorcycles model page - TE 300 2024

topic: no map switch on GasGas TPI 300s
statement: The 2022 GasGas EX 300 and EC 300 TPI come without the two-position map switch that the KTM and Husqvarna versions carry; testers did not miss it because the TPI engines are manageable as they are.

source.name: Cycle News - 2022 GasGas EX 300 review

topic: map switch effect on the 2021 TE 300i
statement: A tester found the difference between the two map-switch positions on the 2021 TE 300i negligible and blamed a slightly lean feel at speed on the factory emissions tune.

source.name: Cycle News - 2021 Husqvarna TE 300i review

topic: map switch and fuel system on the 2020 TX 300i
statement: The 2020 TX 300i has a two-position switch on the throttle side - two hash marks mellow, one hash mark aggressive (reversed from earlier Husqvarnas); the 39 mm throttle body meters only air so there is no jetting, and it needs injector-compatible two-stroke oil in a 700 cc tank. The importer advised against adjusting the power valve.
notes: The owner's manual lists the oil tank as approx. 0.6 l.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test: 2020 Husqvarna TX300i

statement: KTM's 2024 XC-W range moved to throttle-body injection (39 mm Keihin) with an electronic power valve, electronic oil injection and new reed-case flaps, an independent Off-road Control Unit under the seat, a frame with parallel engine mounts and a forged shock mount, a hybrid polyamide/aluminium subframe, a hollow die-cast swingarm, WP XACT closed-cartridge fork and a redesigned WP XPLOR shock.
notes: Manufacturer release as reported.

source.name: Cycle News - New 2024 KTM XC-W two-stroke off-road model specs (KTM release)

statement: For 2026 the KTM enduro range got refreshed graphics, new damping settings with lighter, shorter fork springs and a reworked shock reservoir, a protection cap on the fuel connector against dirt and water, and a radiator cap with a standard thread.
notes: Range-wide statements in the release; model-specific attribution is implied.

source.name: Cycle News - New 2026 KTM XC-W enduro specs (KTM release)

statement: Husqvarna's 2026 TX 300 got threaded radiator caps, a fuel-line protection cap and new graphics; it keeps the 293 cc TBI engine with electronic exhaust control, 1:60 premix, 26:72 primary, 14:48 final drive and WP XACT closed-cartridge fork, at about 224.8 lb without fuel.

source.name: Cycle News - New 2026 Husqvarna TC, FX, TX specs (Husqvarna release)

statement: GasGas's 2026 update brought black rims and a style refresh; the EC 300 got new WP XPLOR/XACT settings, a radiator fan (now on all enduro models), rerouted two-stroke wiring harnesses and a softer tire compound, and the enduro line-up shrank to the EC 300, EC 350F and EC 500F. The EX 300 keeps ECU settings that differ from the MC models.
notes: Manufacturer release as reported; EX-specific attribution limited.

source.name: Enduro21 - First look 2026 GASGAS off-road range

statement: KTM's 2027 XC range is largely unchanged, with proven engines and six-speed gearboxes, the 125 XC back in the line-up, WP XACT closed-cartridge fork and XACT shock, and new in-mold graphics with red tank-shroud highlights.

source.name: Enduro21 - Quick look 2027 KTM XC and XC-F range

statement: KTM said the 2022 125 XC got a 50-tooth rear sprocket for more top speed, a direct result of customer feedback, with otherwise unchanged engine and chassis.
notes: The 2022 owner's manual still lists 13:51 for all 125 models - see conflicts.

source.name: Enduro21 - First look 2022 KTM cross-country and motocross models

statement: Husqvarna's 2024 TE 300 got a refined chromoly frame with a new shock mount no longer tied to the main tube for better anti-squat, an all-new WP XACT shock 100 g lighter and 15 mm shorter, a swingarm 190 g lighter, and an engine over 1.2 kg lighter than the previous generation.

source.name: Husqvarna Motorcycles model page - TE 300 2024

statement: Testers found the 300 XC-W shares the 250's chassis but turns slightly less quickly because of its extra rotating mass; the 150 is the lightest-feeling, and a steering damper was suggested for high sixth-gear speeds on rough ground.

source.name: Ultimate Motorcycling - 2024 KTM XC-W lineup test (300, 250 and 150 reviewed)

statement: KTM says the 2026 300 XC-W keeps the 48 mm WP XACT closed-cartridge fork with new, shorter and lighter main springs, while the PDS shock has no hardware changes; both ends have tool-free clickers.
notes: The 2026 release describes the spring/damping update as range-wide.

source.name: KTM USA model page - 2026 KTM 300 XC-W

statement: Testers found the 2024 150 XC-W suspension softer and plusher than the 250/300, while the 250/300 resisted bottoming and stayed consistent when pushed; the 150 needs more shifting because its clutch has no damping function.

source.name: Ultimate Motorcycling - 2024 KTM XC-W lineup test (300, 250 and 150 reviewed)

statement: For motocross-style riding testers ran the 2020 TX 300i air fork at 145 psi (stock 139), 12 clicks out compression and rebound, fork on the 3rd line; shock 42 N/mm spring, high-speed compression 1-1/4 turns out, low-speed 8 clicks, rebound 14 clicks, 105 mm race sag (102-108 mm sweet spot). Raising the forks cured front-end push.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test: 2020 Husqvarna TX300i

topic: suspension baseline notes: 2022 GasGas EX 300 / EC 300
statement: Testers found the 2022 EX 300's WP XACT air fork and shock jarringly stiff out of the box for trail use and needing constant attention, while the EC 300's coil-spring XPLOR suspension is trail-oriented and suits riders up to about 170 lb.
notes: EC statement from the companion EC 300 review.

source.name: Cycle News - 2022 GasGas EX 300 review

statement: A 165 lb tester found the 2021 TE 300i coil-spring XPLOR suspension cushy and excellent in rocks, but likely too soft for heavier riders or aggressive high-speed riding.

source.name: Cycle News - 2021 Husqvarna TE 300i review

topic: 2020 TX 300i fuel cut-out when low on fuel
statement: Testers found that whipping the 2020 TX 300i left-side-up while low on fuel could make the engine quit, a fuel-pickup issue; they also disliked the 18-inch AT81 rear tire for motocross.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test: 2020 Husqvarna TX300i

source.name: Cycle News - 2021 Husqvarna TE 300i review

topic: 2022 GasGas EC 300 front brake and protection
statement: Testers found the 2022 EC 300 front brake the weak point (firm lever but less stopping power than the Brembo/Magura siblings) and noted it comes without handguards or a skid plate; range is about 100 miles of mellow trail from the 2.3 gal tank.

source.name: Cycle News - 2022 GasGas EC 300 review

statement: Testers noted the 2022 EX 300 comes without handguards or a skid plate, has vulnerable exhaust pipes and an air fork needing frequent checks, and showed lean spots before full temperature.

source.name: Cycle News - 2022 GasGas EX 300 review

statement: A 2020 250 XC TPI owner reported a spluttery engine at part throttle from low to mid rpm with a flat top end and signs of rich running; the magazine recommends checking the throttle-body air screw and getting the latest ECU settings from the dealer first.

source.name: Dirt Bike Magazine - KTM 250 TPI issues and solutions (Mr. Know-It-All)

source.name: Enduro21 - First look 2026 GASGAS off-road range

source.name: KTM South Africa model page - 2027 KTM 300 XC

source.name: Dirt Rider - 2024 GasGas EX 300 dyno test (Dynojet 250i)
